reviews.reason: The retrieved root-assessment@1 already supplies the requested bounded precursor: paid examination of an identified planted specimen, dated personal evidence, retained physical work and explicit limits on inference. Related placement, site and prepared-surface capabilities do not establish biological viability or propagation. The request expressly permits unknown findings, so neither a new viability mechanism nor duplicate assessment development is necessary. Persistence of the original specimen is not proof of viability; elapsed observation rounds are not proof of growth, deterioration or death.
reviews.experienceReview: Assessment, learning, requests, naming and reaching an observation interval do not themselves earn pleasure or satisfaction. Repeated unchanged findings earn no information-gain benefit. A genuinely informative observed change or informative negative result may be considered only by the existing single grounded-understanding/evidence-deduplicated rule, with personal applicability, its existing bounded amount, cap, decay and cooldown; this reuse adds no reward rule or separate reward for the same evidence. An unsupported or inconclusive query alone is not verified information gain. No comfort, nutrition, health or energy restoration is supplied. Protected reward accounts, budgets, goals and permissions remain unchanged.
reviews.visualReview: Keep functional evidence distinct from presentation and experience. Reuse the actual root plot's plant component and existing appearance; use observable work events and retained exposure/progress to distinguish examination begun, uncovered, interrupted, covered and completed findings. Evidence metadata should reference the target ID, processId, tick, method, completed stage and supported finding or unknown status so it can be reused without implying a new physical effect. A covered plot or completed inspection must not display germination, a viable-plant badge, food, propagation or a successful diagnosis unsupported by observation. Failed access produces no examination-success event; interrupted inspection may show only the exposure and work actually completed. Public visuals disclose only observable physical events, not Moss's private report or concealed specimen properties.
reviews.specification: Reuse root-assessment@1, handler long.root-assessment, equivalence planted-root:paid-inspection:1; record this reuse rather than claiming a new implementation. Use its existing modes begin, observe, inspect, resume and cancel. Require an explicit exact target, either root-trial-10-moss-48 or root-trial-101-moss-602, and validate current physical reach and access before examination; a remembered record or target name alone is insufficient. Each plot is examined separately. Only the creator may handle a plot; reachable public-state observation does not authorize handling. No prerequisite abilities, resources or knowledge dependencies are declared, but Moss must individually complete the existing learning requirement; this review grants neither mastery nor execution. Begin/observe costs one actual round and 0.2 energy. Begin records an external baseline and claims the personal work lock. Inspect costs two paid work rounds at one energy each, uncovering the existing reserved specimen, recording its actually accessible condition and replacing the displaced soil. No tools, water, replacement root or consumable sampling materials are supplied or required. Do not add destructive cutting, extraction or laboratory testing to this version. Preserve the original specimen identity, provenance and all displaced soil; output is evidence, not new matter, edible stock, fertility or biomass. Reports must carry the execution tick, target and available input-item/provenance references, examination method, actual exposure, completed work and observational limits. Distinguish original specimen present, directly observed deterioration, directly observed new structure, and unresolved identity or condition only as supported by accessible evidence; absence of represented evidence is not evidence of absence. Do not infer that an additional structure is an independent propagated plant or that a persistent root is alive. The older root's earlier finding of only the original specimen remains a historical observation, not a current finding. The second plot's surface-38-moss-234 association is not a viability certificate. When the examination cannot resolve viability, new growth or propagation, report unknown explicitly. Retain exact plot, processId, remaining inspection rounds, exposure and paid effort across interruption; resume revalidates access and pays only outstanding work. Explicit cancel or death settles the lock once without automatically covering exposed material or refunding spent energy/time. Cancellation does not convert the planted root into inventory. Existing specimen ageing continues while unattended, including while exposed; disclose the physical disturbance and exposure risk without inventing a risk probability. Completed evidence and physical changes persist. No passive assessment, tending effect, automatic reinspection or maintenance benefit is created. Further examination requires another actual paid action. Personal evidence is shared only through actual communication; other participants must act independently. Development/review waiting advances no world time. Established checks, accounting, progress and evidence limitations execute in the existing code, not repeated model adjudication.
